clue.text: Understood American historian of the ancient world

parts.note: tacit means understood without being spoken

explanation.surface: An American scholar of antiquity whose meaning is taken as read.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacitus was a Roman historian, author of the Annals and Histories.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman senator who chronicled the early empire, so he is an ancient historian.

clue.text: Where pigs may be going, that's cosy and warm

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as three words: heading towards a pigsty, the pen where pigs are kept
second meaning: snug and comfortably warm

explanation.surface: A pigsty is a snug, warm place for the animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as TO A STY, it describes where pigs head.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is informal for comfortably warm, like being toasted by a fire.

clue.text: King, tucking into fried food, sends out tweets

indicators.note: tucking into means the king's letter goes inside the fried food

parts.note: chips are fried potato strips

explanation.surface: A monarch eats fries while posting on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' looks like eating, but it means placing inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds chirp to make short high calls, which is what a bird's tweets are.

clue.text: Rugby scores from urban areas in Holland, as Spooner says

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so these two words trade their starts
says points to the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: things in Holland are Dutch; said aloud the word rhymes with the answer's first part
towns are urban areas

explanation.surface: Points in a rugby match come from Dutch cities, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch towns, with their opening sounds swapped, becomes touch downs.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchdown is the grounding of the ball behind the line that scores a try in rugby.

clue.text: Personnel in U-boat getting broom, say

indicators.note: in places the personnel letters inside the submarine

parts.note: a U-boat is a German submarine, a sub
HR, human resources, is the modern name for the personnel department

explanation.surface: Submarine crew grab a broom for cleaning duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Broom is a yellow-flowered bush, not a sweeping brush.
explanation.definitionFit: Broom is a flowering bush of the pea family, an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Quirky like a bobby having a rest?

definitions.text: like a bobby having a rest?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a police officer off duty is off his beat, the street patrol route

explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British police officer, and his beat is the area he patrols on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat describes something unusual or unconventional, close in sense to eccentric.

clue.text: Masters a bit of cricket by place where it's played

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
Lord's is the famous London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Experts in a portion of a cricket match by its venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's in London is known as the home of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are rulers with supreme power over others, hence masters.

clue.text: Supporter defending United, a goatish fellow

indicators.note: defending suggests the fan surrounds and protects the team letter

parts.note: a fan supports a team

explanation.surface: A football fan stands up for Manchester United and acts like a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A faun is a Roman rural deity, half man and half goat.

clue.text: Demanding old lover with lawsuit

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
an action is a case in court

explanation.surface: A demanding former partner who files a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaction is the act of demanding payment or compliance, a noun matching demanding as a gerund.

clue.text: Eccentric stayed with us in parts of the week

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball lodged with us for a few days.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuesday is one of the seven days that make up a calendar week.

clue.text: I'm leaving university, following crazy idea

indicators.note: following means the university letter comes after the jumbled idea
crazy suggests the word idea has gone haywire, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A student quits college after hatching a mad scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French farewell, said by someone departing, so it stands for a goodbye announcement.

clue.text: Crude tea brewed by head of Eton school again

indicators.note: tea that is brewed is stirred up, so these letters are mixed into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: The headmaster of Eton makes a rough cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English private boarding school, which supports the school setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is to teach, so to reeducate is to teach someone a second time.

clue.text: Work in tense police series? Take a starring role

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
The Bill was a long-running British TV police drama

explanation.surface: An actor lands the lead in a gripping cop show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bill is a British police drama that ran for decades on ITV; 'the bill' is also slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever tops the bill is named first on the poster, the headline performer in a show.

clue.text: Learners getting 50% off an earring

indicators.note: losing half the word, so only the first four of its eight letters stay

parts.note: students are learners

explanation.surface: Pupils get a half-price deal on jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a small ear ornament fixed through the lobe, one kind of earring.

clue.text: Jeering Republican interrupts Obama during start of gala

indicators.note: interrupts means the Republican letter breaks into the president's name

parts.note: Barack is Obama's first name
during can mean in, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A Republican heckles Obama at the opening of a gala.
explanation.walkthrough: Barracking is British for jeering or heckling a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to shout abuse or heckle, so barracking is jeering at someone.

clue.text: Two right-wingers hosting wild raves in sunny room

indicators.note: hosting means the two political words hold the other letters between them

parts.note: con and Tory are both short for a Conservative

indicators.note: wild indicates the word raves is scrambled

explanation.surface: A pair of Tories throw a rave party in a glazed extension.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory and Con both mean a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatory is a glass-walled room attached to a house, built to catch the sunlight.

clue.text: Some in Windies team bat heroically in sweaty environment

indicators.note: some of the letters in these words make up the answer

parts.note: the answer runs across these words, from the end of Windies to the start of heroically

explanation.surface: The West Indies side battle valiantly in humid heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Windies is a nickname for the West Indies cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam bath is a hot vapour-filled room meant to make you perspire.

clue.text: Hindrance that stops cruel cats bounding up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the answer stops, or stays put, inside the run of words that follow

parts.note: the answer lies across these words, from the end of cruel to the start of bounding

explanation.surface: Something blocks vicious cats from leaping upward.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'cruel cats bounding' and are then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is a barrier or impediment that blocks progress.

clue.text: Jim almost welcoming dullard in grand party

indicators.note: welcoming means the shortened name takes the dullard inside it
almost means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Jim is a short form of James
a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: Jim nearly lets a dreary guest into his lavish celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large festive gathering, such as a big celebration or rally.

clue.text: Sinatra's confused with beer and cryptic crosswords, say

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of these words are muddled

explanation.surface: Sinatra mixed up after drinking, struggling over crossword puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic crosswords are examples of puzzles that challenge the mind, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Extravagant whiskey drunk by sober people in capital city

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extravagant

indicators.note: drunk by means swallowed, so the whiskey letter sits inside the sober people

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members stay sober
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Teetotallers lavishly downing whiskey in a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital of Canada.

clue.text: Stick marketing material in this place

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Put the advertising poster up right here.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain attached, a synonym of the verb to stick.

clue.text: London transport still heading west, then east

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means read right to left

parts.note: still can mean but, as in 'still, it was fun'

explanation.surface: The capital's trains still run westward, then turn east.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the nickname for the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tube is the popular name for the London Underground railway system.

clue.text: Troublemaker with funny dialect is incriminated

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or sprite

indicators.note: funny here suggests the word dialect behaving oddly, so it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker with a comic accent is found guilty by association.
explanation.definitionFit: To be implicated in wrongdoing is to be shown to be involved in it, a synonym of incriminated.

clue.text: Friend upset by case of severe blunder

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters

parts.note: its outer letters, first and last, are used

explanation.surface: A mate is distressed by a serious mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor error, a kind of blunder.

clue.text: Two areas around southern India — in this region?

indicators.note: around means the two area letters surround the others

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for area, doubled here

explanation.surface: Two zones flanking southern India, asking if they are part of a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the continent that contains India, so the region in question.

clue.text: One guilty of dodgy dealing when giving others a hand?

definitions.text: One guilty of dodgy dealing when giving others a hand?

parts.words: One guilty of dodgy dealing when giving others a hand
parts.note: reads as a crooked helper, but the hand is a set of playing cards a cheat deals out

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a crooked helper; the hand is a set of playing cards dealt out by a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a professional cheat at card games, swindling other players at the table.

clue.text: Furious criminal in the main losing power

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the seafaring criminal

parts.note: the main is the open sea, where a pirate operates

explanation.surface: A seagoing outlaw rages after his strength deserts him.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, a direct synonym of furious.

clue.text: Rot in English tree remains after burning

parts.note: the yew is an evergreen tree
ash is what is left once something burns

explanation.surface: Decay in an English tree leaves only cinders behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Rot here is nonsense, not decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for nonsense or humbug, the same sense as rot meaning rubbish talk.

clue.text: Do some carving in French tomb

parts.note: en is French for in
a grave is a burial place

explanation.surface: Chiselling inscriptions inside a French burial chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut letters or designs into a hard surface, a kind of carving.
